newsitem.title: UK: S&P cuts Credit Suisse, ups CS First.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Credit Suisse, ups CS First.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it cut the long-term debt ratings of Credit Suisse and related entities, and Credit Suisse Financial Products to AA from AA plus.
At the same time, it raised the long-term debt ratings of CS First Boston Inc to AA from A and the short-term ratings to A1 plus from A1.
"The outlooks are stable," S&P said in a statement.
S&P said it also assigned AA minus/A1 plus counterparty ratings to the Credit Suisse Group (formerly CS Holding) and the 'new' Credit Suisse (formerly Swiss Volksbank).
CS First Boston's counterparty ratings are withdrawn and the ratings fo Credit Suisse, CSFP and CS First Boston Ince are removed from CreditWatch, S&P said.
The rating action follows the finalisation of the restructuring first announced in July 1996 by CS Holding, the parent of AA plus rated Credit Suisse, CSFP and CS First Boston Inc, S&P said.

"Under the restructuring, the investment bank, CS First Boston Inc, will be integrated with CSFP, and the institutional asset management and corporate and investment activities of Credit Suisse, which will change its name to Credit Suisse Frist Boston" S&P said.
Simultaneously, a 'new' Credit Suisse bank will be established to conduct the existing retail and private banking activities of Credit Suisse, S&P said.
In addition, the parent company, CS Holding, will change its name to Credit Suisse Group. The group will begin operating under the new structure on January 1, 1997, it said.
S&P said the outstanding debt of Credit Suisse and Credit Suisse Financial Products will remain with the existing legal entities.
However, it said the downgrade reflects the transfer of the substantial private banking operations of the current Credit Suisse to the "new' Credit Suisse.
"Consequently the risk profile of the new Credit Suisse First Boston is greater than the existing Credit Suisse," the agency.
CS First Boston's upgrade reflects its integration into the new Credit Suisse First Boston, which has a lower risk profile.
